text:
kate: CI publish to our registry is failing on main during the final manifest push. buildkite job https://buildkite.com/redwood/pipeline/builds/4567 shows 

Error excerpt:
```
Pushing manifest to registry...
manifest validation failed: layer sha256:abc123 expected digest sha256:abc123 but got sha256:def456
remote: manifest invalid: digest mismatch
error: failed to upload manifest
```

I didn't touch the image layers intentionally — last relevant merge was a rebase of feature/fast-start. Anyone seen a manifest/digest flip like this recently? :eyes:

miguel: Can you paste the full push log (with the layer digests)? Also which Dockerfile stage changed in the rebase? My first thought: context tar/order/mtime causing reproducible-diff in layer tarballs, or a build cache poisoning a layer.

kate: Full log attached in the job; key lines look like:
```
layer 1: sha256:aaa111 size=2.1MB
layer 2: sha256:bbb222 size=14.8MB
layer 3: sha256:abc123 size=512KB  <-- registry expected
registry response: got sha256:def456 for layer 3
```

sara: I rebased that branch and had to change a small COPY for permissions. I also ran local buildx with cache, then pushed. I didn't set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or tar options. Could be that my local build produced a slightly different tar header order.

alex: Try two quick checks to narrow it down:
1) Re-run the publish job with --no-cache/BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0 so it rebuilds all layers deterministically. If that fixes it, cache divergence is likely.
2) Use skopeo to inspect both manifests/raw blobs from the registry and the local image to compare raw digests:
```
skopeo inspect --raw docker://registry.internal/redwood/myimage:canary > remote_raw.json
docker save myimage:local | sha256sum
```
If the remote raw manifest references a blob digest that doesn't exist or points to a different blob, that'll prove a registry mismatch.

miguel: Also try `docker build --no-cache --pull --progress=plain` and then `docker save` and `sha256sum` of the tar to compare with what was pushed. If tar headers are the cause, a reproducible tar with `--mtime` and normalized owners helps. Example workaround in the build step: set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` and add a small script to create the context tar with `tar --sort=name --mtime='1970-01-01' --owner=0 --group=0 -cf context.tar .` and feed that to buildx via `--remote-context`. Ugly but useful to test.

sara: I'll try `--no-cache` and the deterministic tar trick locally. If it reproduces, we can add deterministic context to CI.

buildkite: Re-run requested by @kate: https://buildkite.com/redwood/pipeline/builds/4568 (no-cache flag added).

kate: Thanks. If the no-cache re-run passes, we can blame cache divergence and schedule a follow-up to harden reproducibility. If it still fails, we'll bisect commits between main@{yesterday}..main@{now} and run `docker build` per commit to find the offending diff. I'll ping @miguel to help with bisect if needed. :thumbsup:

alex: If you need a quick manual upload to narrow registry vs client, I can `skopeo copy` the local image tar to the registry and confirm whether the registry accepts it or rejects it. That will tell us if the registry is mis-indexing blobs.

kate: Good plan. I'll update here after the re-run completes.

sara: quick note — I also pushed a tiny commit that flips file mode on one copied file in the Dockerfile (chmod +x). Might be related. Will pause merges until we confirm.

kate: appreciated.
